extracted.intended_audience: federal agency regulatory analysts and economists preparing regulatory analyses
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for estimating and applying the social rate of time preference (SRTP) for U.S. federal regulatory analyses, including near-term (30-year) estimates, corresponding discount factors, and a modeled long-term schedule over a 150-year horizon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This Appendix is updated every three years. This version of the Appendix is valid until the release of a subsequent Appendix in 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may generally continue to refer to the discount rate estimate in the version of the Appendix in effect at the time that a regulatory analysis for a proposed regulation is received by OMB, even if the Appendix is updated before the regulation is finalized. However, if the Appendix has been updated more than once since the proposed regulation was received by OMB, agencies should refer to the most recent version of the Appendix. Electronic copies and links to the Circular and historical rates are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Near-term SRTP estimation (next 30 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB estimates the social rate of time preference (SRTP) over the next 30 years by considering the 30-year average (currently covering 1993 to 2022) of the yield on 10-year Treasury marketable securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the yield on 10-year TIPS (measuring inflation by CPI) for years TIPS are available (2003–2022). For years without TIPS (1993–2002), use the yield on 10-year Treasury notes minus the average annual rate of change in the CPI. Then add 0.3 percentage points to reflect inflation as measured by the PCE inflation index rather than CPI. For the current Appendix: 30-year securities average = 1.7 percent; PCE inflation adjustment = 0.3 percent; resulting SRTP estimate = 2.0 percent. See the Explanation and Response to Public Input document for more details on selection of data and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount factors for first 30 years (apply 2.0% SRTP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding discount factors over the next 30 years using 2.0 percent per year are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided year-by-year discount factors when applying the 2.0% SRTP in regulatory benefit–cost calculations. The Appendix supplies the full table for years 1–30 (selected values shown): Year 1 = 0.9804, Year 2 = 0.9612, Year 3 = 0.9423, ... Year 15 = 0.7430, ... Year 30 = 0.5521. (Use the complete table in the Appendix for precise values.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term SRTP estimation methodology (beyond 30 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB models the discount rate in each year beyond the next 30 years as the sum of a slow-moving trend component (a random walk) and a cyclical component (an AR(1) process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model details and parameters: innovations in the random walk are normally distributed with mean zero and variance 0.04; the cyclical component is AR(1) with AR parameter 0.7 and innovations normally distributed with mean zero and variance 0.9. Constrain rates to be non-negative each year. Simulate 100,000 paths for the discount rate, calculate the expected discount factor across these paths, and compute forward rates consistent with that path of expected discount factors. OMB provides rates on a 150-year horizon; see the Explanation and Response to Public Input for fuller rationale and methodological detail. Rates beyond 150 years are available from OMB upon agency request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default long-term discount rate schedule (150-year horizon)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB provides a default schedule of discount rates by multi-year ranges for years beyond the initial 30-year near-term period up to the 150-year horizon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Appendix lists the default schedule (example current values): Years 2023–2079: 2.0%; 2080–2094: 1.9%; 2095–2105: 1.8%; 2106–2115: 1.7%; 2116–2125: 1.6%; 2126–2134: 1.5%; 2135–2143: 1.4%; 2144–2153: 1.3%; 2154–2163: 1.2%; 2164–2172: 1.1%. Agencies should apply these scheduled rates for the specified year ranges when conducting long-term regulatory discounting unless using alternative, justified rates and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: References and availability of supporting documents and historical rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Appendix references and provides links to supporting documents: the full Circular A-4 text, an Explanation and Response to Public Input, and a table of past years’ rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain electronic copies from the provided White House links (CircularA-4Appendix.pdf, CircularA-4.pdf, CircularA-4DiscountHistory.pdf). Use the Explanation document for more details on selection of data, rationale, and methodology. Agencies may request rates extending beyond the 150-year schedule from OMB.
